preamble: In seven of the clues the definition element does not lead to the whole solution; a 14 27 needs to be added first to produce the required grid entry.

clue.text: Leggy creature's independent musical direction

parts.note: bis is a score marking telling players to repeat a passage

explanation.surface: Someone long-limbed shows a free spirit in how they take musical direction.
explanation.definitionFit: The ibis is a wading bird with long thin legs, so it is fairly described as a leggy animal.

clue.text: Before court cut short stir-crazy tough

indicators.note: Before places the scrambled stir ahead of the court piece
crazy says the letters of stir are thrown into disorder

parts.note: court shortened gives its abbreviation CT

explanation.surface: A prisoner, about to face the bench, goes stir-crazy under a harsh regime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stir-crazy' reads as one word, but 'stir' is fodder and 'crazy' turns it into STRI.
explanation.definitionFit: Strict and tough are synonyms when describing a hard, uncompromising regime or person.

clue.text: Flowers, jar version, collapsed

indicators.note: collapsed says the letters of jar version have fallen into a new order

explanation.surface: A vase of flowers lies broken after the jar gave way.
explanation.walkthrough: One of the seven themed clues: 'Flowers' defines only RIVERS, and the preamble's female name JOAN goes in front, giving the American comedian Joan Rivers.
explanation.definitionFit: Rivers flow, so a flower in crossword terms is a river; prefixing the woman's name JOAN gives the comedian's full name.

clue.text: Prejudicial to those getting on revolving stage without electric current

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the turned stage surrounds the current
revolving says the letters of stage turn round, the front pair moving to the back

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Old performers find the revolving stage, left without power, a bias against them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolving' cycles STAGE to AGEST, and 'without' wraps it round I.
explanation.definitionFit: Ageism is discrimination by age, so an attitude biased against older people is described this way.

clue.text: Line taken by persistent sort (fusspot)

indicators.note: taken by means the line is absorbed into the persistent sort

parts.note: a sticker is someone who keeps going and will not give up

explanation.surface: A dogged person toes the line, being rather pernickety.
explanation.definitionFit: A stickler insists on exactness about details, which is what a fusspot does.

clue.text: Slasher's legacy: second estate?

parts.note: an estate is a British name for a station wagon, a kind of car

explanation.surface: A knife attacker leaves a mark, or perhaps a second property.
explanation.walkthrough: An estate in Britain is an estate car, a station wagon.
explanation.definitionFit: A slashing wound heals into a lasting mark, the mark left behind by the attacker.

clue.text: Flash stuff in Bengal circles

indicators.note: circles says the letters of in Bengal go round into a new order

explanation.surface: Showy jewellery is worn across the districts of Bengal.
explanation.walkthrough: A themed clue: 'Flash stuff' defines only BLING, and the female name ENA is put in front of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Bling is slang for flashy jewellery; adding the woman's name ENA in front makes the entry, which means making possible.

clue.text: Finished taming ego of Gordon

indicators.note: taming suggests breaking something wild into a new shape, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone has broken the arrogance of a man called Gordon.
explanation.definitionFit: Something permanently over and done with is finished, never to return.

clue.text: Love, old — nevertheless getting into punt

indicators.note: getting into says one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a punt is a bet or wager
though can mean nevertheless, as in 'he came, though'

explanation.surface: An old romance that still found its way onto a boat on the river.
explanation.walkthrough: A themed clue: 'Love, old' defines only OUGHT, an archaic word for nought, and the female name BETH goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Ought is an old spelling of nought, zero or love in tennis; with BETH in front the entry is an archaic verb meaning considered.

clue.text: Part of poem's affected style of speech and poetic interjection

parts.note: cant is hypocritical or affected talk
O is the exclamation found in verse, as in 'O Romeo'

explanation.surface: A section of verse shows a mannered diction and an exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: A canto is one of the major divisions of a long poem such as Dante's.

clue.text: Endless row backing housing chief's main descendant

indicators.note: housing says the reversed row holds the next piece inside it
backing says the shortened row is read backwards
Endless says the last letter of the word for row is dropped

parts.note: a row is a loud noise or din

indicators.note: the main, leading letter of chief is its first

explanation.surface: A din at the back hides who will inherit the clan leader's estate.
explanation.walkthrough: NOISE loses its end to give NOIS, which 'backing' turns to SION, then that holds C.
explanation.definitionFit: A scion is an heir or offspring of a family, especially a notable one.

clue.text: Dyed-in-the-wool Conservative spiking Labour, ie swapping nitrogen for oxygen

indicators.note: spiking means the Conservative is driven into the other letters
swapping says the letters are exchanged among themselves into a new order
nitrogen for oxygen means the letter for one element replaces the other

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
O is the chemical symbol of oxygen
N is the chemical symbol of nitrogen

explanation.surface: A political chemistry lesson: a staunch Tory infiltrates Labour, swapping elements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swapping' could also read as the element exchange, but 'for' already signals that; 'swapping' then rearranges the letters, and 'spiking' drives C into the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Dyed-in-the-wool describes someone fixed in their ways beyond any cure, so beyond remedy.

clue.text: Disturbance makes state chamber musicians tense

parts.note: PA is the postal abbreviation of the US state Pennsylvania
a trio is a small chamber group of three players
T is the grammar abbreviation of tense

explanation.surface: A row breaks out when a state's chamber players get tense.
explanation.walkthrough: A themed clue: 'Disturbance' defines only RIOT, and the female name PAT goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: A riot is a violent public disturbance; prefixing the name PAT gives a lover of their country.

clue.text: Pressure put on naff chat shows piece

indicators.note: put on places the pressure on top of the next piece in this down light

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure

indicators.note: naff, British slang for poor or tacky, says the letters of chat are rearranged

explanation.surface: Under pressure, a dreary talk show screens a short segment.
explanation.definitionFit: A patch is a small piece of material, or a piece of ground.

clue.text: Like a male ballroom dancer requesting "no piano"?

indicators.note: no says the piano letter is removed

parts.note: pleading means asking or requesting
P is the music abbreviation for piano, meaning softly

explanation.surface: A man on the dance floor begs the band to stop the piano.
explanation.definitionFit: In ballroom dancing the man traditionally guides his partner, taking the front role.

clue.text: Lebanon produced and raised New York State's ultimate old queen

indicators.note: produced, in the sense of brought out in a new form, says the letters of Lebanon are rearranged
ultimate picks the last letter of State's
raised in a down light means read upwards, so backwards

explanation.surface: A Middle Eastern country and New York State join to promote a monarch of old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'produced' turns LEBANON into ANNEBOL, and 'raised' turns NY to YN.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry VIII's second wife was a Tudor queen consort, beheaded in 1536.

clue.text: Good shot sorted out invaders

indicators.note: sorted out says the letters of shot are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A fine hit sees off a band of attackers.
explanation.definitionFit: The Goths were Germanic peoples who invaded the Roman Empire.

clue.text: Two Russian doll-like articles between freeman and noble

indicators.note: Russian dolls nest one inside the other, so one article sits inside the other

parts.note: the definite article is THE
two articles are meant, AN being the smaller of them

explanation.surface: A pair of Russian dolls ranks somewhere in the middle of feudal society.
explanation.walkthrough: The two articles are THE and AN, nested like Russian dolls.
explanation.definitionFit: In Anglo-Saxon England a thane held land from the king, ranking above an ordinary freeman but below a hereditary noble.

clue.text: Article: neuter cat for a fraction of a pound

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
N is the grammar abbreviation of neuter
the ounce is another name for the snow leopard

explanation.surface: Having a pet cat neutered costs only a few pence.
explanation.walkthrough: A themed clue: 'a fraction of a pound' defines only OUNCE, and the female name ANN goes in front, giving a verb meaning proclaim.
explanation.definitionFit: An ounce is one sixteenth of an avoirdupois pound; the woman's name ANN in front makes a verb meaning to declare.

clue.text: See 8
Window nut, easily moved

parts.note: a nut is an enthusiast or fan
light things weigh little and are easily moved

explanation.surface: A window fitting with a loose nut rattles about.
explanation.definitionFit: A fanlight is a semicircular window above a door.

clue.text: Slight inversion round fang tip preferred by Dracula

indicators.note: round says the reversed word goes about the next letter
inversion means the word for slight is turned round, read backwards

parts.note: slight means thin or slender

indicators.note: the tip of a fang is its end, the last letter

explanation.surface: A vampire's fang just grazes its victim.
explanation.walkthrough: THIN reversed is NIHT, which goes round G, the end of 'fang'.
explanation.definitionFit: Vampires shun daylight, so the dark hours are when Dracula prefers to be out.

clue.text: Student's touching approach?

parts.note: a practical, learn-by-doing method, as if the learner literally puts his ... the work

explanation.definitionFit: Hands-on learning is practical and involves direct involvement, physically touching the materials.

clue.text: Be thankful for indulgent sort at bar

parts.note: the biblical Job is the type of forbearing patience
bar and less both mean except, as in 'all bar one'

explanation.surface: A drinker is grateful to find a tolerant person at the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: A themed clue: 'Be thankful for' defines only BLESS, and the female name JO goes in front, making a word meaning out of work.
explanation.definitionFit: To bless can mean to be grateful for, as in 'I bless the day'; JO prefixed gives the entry.

clue.text: Keep recycling articles as an entertainer?

definitions.text: Keep recycling articles as an entertainer?

parts.words: Keep recycling articles as an entertainer?
parts.note: a performer who keeps several items going round in the air, catching and tossing them again

explanation.definitionFit: To juggle is to keep objects continuously thrown and caught, as a circus performer does.

clue.text: Take on Scouse MP, loyalist at heart

indicators.note: at heart says the letters are found in the middle of the words Scouse MP loyalist

explanation.surface: A Liverpool politician hires a party faithful.
explanation.definitionFit: To employ someone is to hire them, to take them on staff.

clue.text: Little animal, little weight, littlest one attended by Erica?

indicators.note: attended by says the next piece accompanies the one before it

parts.note: G, for gram, is a small unit of weight
the runt is the smallest of a litter
Erica is the botanical genus of heather, and ling is a common heather

explanation.surface: A tiny creature, the smallest of the litter, is looked after by a woman named Erica.
explanation.walkthrough: Erica looks like a woman's name but is the Latin name of the heather genus; ling is a heather.
explanation.definitionFit: A gruntling is a young pig, a small animal that grunts.

clue.text: See 8
Salt neutral lake

parts.note: a salt and a tar are both old words for a sailor
N is the abbreviation of neutral, as on a gear stick

explanation.surface: A salty, neutral body of water.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarn is a small mountain lake, especially in the north of England.

clue.text: The beast within lives for a sartorial feature

indicators.note: within says the beast goes inside the other piece

parts.note: lives is the plural of live, and doubling L, the abbreviation of live, makes the plural
an ape is a beast

explanation.surface: A tailor says there is something animal inside each of us.
explanation.walkthrough: Doubling a letter makes a plural in abbreviations (pp for pages), so 'lives' gives LL.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapel is the folded flap on the front of a jacket, a detail of tailoring.

clue.text: Title song about diamonds

indicators.note: about says the song goes around the diamonds

parts.note: a lay is an old word for a song or ballad
D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: A tune called something about diamonds.
explanation.definitionFit: Lady is a title of rank for the wife of a peer or knight.

clue.text: Doctors reckon thousand lost (old money)

indicators.note: doctors as a verb means tampers with, so the letters are rearranged
lost says the thousand letter is taken out

explanation.surface: Medics reckon a thousand pounds has gone missing.
explanation.walkthrough: RECKON less K is RECON, which 'Doctors' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: An oncer was British slang for a one-pound note, a currency item no longer issued.

clue.text: Lloyd who dithers about love deal?

indicators.note: dithers suggests wavering about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A man named Lloyd hesitates over a romantic proposal.
explanation.walkthrough: A themed clue: 'deal' defines only WOOD, deal being pine timber, and the female name HOLLY goes in front, giving the film capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Deal is sawn pine or fir planking, a kind of timber; with HOLLY in front the entry is the Los Angeles film district.
